input.prior_art_strategy: Unchanged this turn. The review recorded source fidelity, formalities, claim structure and numeral consistency as otherwise clean and raised nothing about the claims or the Background, and the finding concerned only the completeness of a schematic recital, so no claim or citation text was touched. Claim 1 still rests on what no reference in the folder teaches: a rigid perimeter member of low-friction material that is not asked to seal, a clearance along at least part of it through which ambient air enters continuously, and an extraction rate sufficient to hold the chamber below atmospheric pressure in spite of that inflow, with every member of the vibration path rigid and the bearing face slidable while the differential is maintained. DE-202021002652-U1 places rubber-elastic suction cup aprons in the vibration path; US-11408462-B2 forms its peripheral wall from elastic partitions and adds a rigid frame only to stop them being drawn inward; US-10001245-B2 abandons vacuum coupling and switches to a blower air cushion in order to move; US-4934475-A uses a seal member and spends its vibration on reducing the adhering force and driving the body along the wall rather than delivering it into the work; US-11247858-B2 lifts sheet articles clear on a perforated suction plate and cleans by suction. Declaring the tile, bonding bed and substrate outlines schematic reinforces that position, because it keeps every shape out of the claimed subject matter.
input.answer: The finding is fixed. The per-figure schematic recitals in the Brief Description of the Drawings now name every element the corresponding brief draws as a declared generic outline: the covering element is added to the FIG. 1, FIG. 2 and FIG. 5 sentences, and the FIG. 4 sentence now recites the perimeter member, the covering element, the bonding material and the substrate. FIG. 3 needed nothing, since its only schematically drawn body was already declared in both places. The edit adds nothing but part names already used in those same sentences and in the numeral table: no shape, proportion, count, "by way of example" phrase or alternative-outline language went into any section, so the application text stays shape-neutral about the tile, the bonding bed and the substrate, matching a disclosure that names them without describing their form. The figure briefs, claims, Detailed Description, Abstract and numeral table are untouched, and all five briefs remain within the character limit.

structured_output.summary: Fixed the single finding by extending the existing "shown schematically" recitals in draft/07-drawings.md so that they reach every element the figure briefs already draw under a declared depiction convention. FIG. 1 now ends "the handle, the vibration motor, the air-extraction mechanism, the base, the perimeter member and the covering element being shown schematically." FIG. 2 now ends "and the air-extraction mechanism, the base, the perimeter member, the covering element and the fluid communication between the air-extraction mechanism and the chamber being shown schematically." FIG. 4 now ends "the perimeter member, the covering element, the bonding material and the substrate being shown schematically." FIG. 5 now ends "and the vibration device, the perimeter member and the covering element being shown schematically." FIG. 3 was left alone, because its only schematically drawn body, the perimeter member, was already declared in both places. Nothing was added but the names of parts that already appear in the numeral table and in these same sentences: no shape, no proportion, no count, no "by way of example" phrase, no optional-outline language, and no new embodiment. The figure briefs, the claims, the Detailed Description, the Abstract and the numeral table are untouched, so the application text remains shape-neutral about the tile, the bonding bed and the substrate, which is all the disclosure supports, since it names them without describing their form. All five briefs remain within the character limit at 2798, 2799, 2531, 2793 and 2788 characters, and the numeral-to-sheet assignments are unchanged: 10, 12, 18, 20, 24, 36, 44 on FIG. 1; 12, 14, 20, 22, 24, 36 on FIG. 2; 16, 24 on FIG. 3; 24, 26, 34, 36, 38, 40, 42 on FIG. 4; 10, 24, 36, 46 on FIG. 5.
reasoning: The gap was between two files that must agree: the briefs declared the tile, the bonding bed and the substrate to be generic outlines, and the Brief Description of the Drawings enumerated schematic elements per figure without naming them. Extending the recital closes the gap in the direction that adds nothing, since 'shown schematically' is a disclaimer of appearance, not an assertion about structure.

I fixed the text rather than the briefs because the briefs are right: the disclosure names the covering element, the bonding material and the substrate and says nothing about their form, so any drawn outline for them is a rendering convention and must be declared as one. Deleting the declarations from the briefs would have left the drawn rectangles undisclaimed, which is the worse of the two directions.

FIG. 3 got no edit. Its brief draws only the perimeter member, already declared schematic in both the brief and the Brief Description, so touching that sentence would have been change for its own sake.

The recitals name parts and stop there. I did not write that the tile is rectangular, that the bands are uniform, or that other forms may be used, because each of those would put appearance into the application text and would be matter the disclosure does not contain.

No claim, description sentence, numeral definition or figure brief changed, so nothing needed resynchronizing beyond the four sentences themselves. The numerals for these parts, 36, 40 and 42, already appear in the Detailed Description and in the numeral table with the same names used in the new recitals.
